subject: Region pinning & data residency - follow-up / next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: John Miller <john.miller@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:10:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: Region pinning & data residency (post-call recap)

Hi John —

Thanks for taking the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we have alignment before the architecture review: 

1) Primary ask: EU data residency for EU customers — all primary inference requests and customer content must remain in an EU region.
2) Cross-region failover: you mentioned acceptable failover behavior where a secondary region can be used for disaster recovery, but only if backups are cold, encrypted with customer-managed keys, and not used for routine processing.
3) Logging and audit: Acme needs audit logs and request logs retained 180 days; access to logs must be available to your security team.
4) PII handling & retention: you asked about default retention for user-provided content (prompt/input) and whether Redwood performs any long-term storage or model training on customer data.
5) Key management / encryption: interest in bringing-your-own KMS for backup encryption and desire for region-scoped keys.

I attached a simple region-pinning diagram and a proposed data-retention table for your review (see attachments). Can you confirm the items above and call out any additional constraints (e.g., specific EU regions, regulatory controls, or procurement timing)?

Next steps we propose:
- We prepare a short architecture diagram (attached) showing per-customer region pinning + cross-region failover pattern.
- Solutions review with your security team (30–45 min) — propose Wed/Thu next week.
- Share SOC2 summary and standard security docs upfront.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: region-pinning-diagram.pdf, data-retention-table.xlsx
From: John Miller <john.miller@acmebank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acmebank.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Region pinning & data residency (post-call recap)

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming and adding some specifics from our side: 

- EU requirement: All primary customer content (requests, responses, derived embeddings, and active KV caches) must stay in EU (ideally eu-west-1 or eu-central-1).
- Cross-region failover: Allowed only for DR. Secondary region (we currently default to us-east-1) may hold encrypted backups. Those backups must be encrypted with a key that we control and never be used for live inference unless explicitly authorized by Acme (manual failover).
- Logging/audit: We need request-level audit logs for 180 days, with an exported copy available to our security team on request. Real-time logging to our SIEM is a plus.
- Retention: Default retention for prompts and user content should be 90 days, with the ability to purge on demand per customer.
- No model training: We cannot allow customer data to be used for model training or any downstream analytics that would persist beyond the retention window.

Can you confirm Redwood supports per-customer region pinning (not just per-tenant but per-route/policy) and whether the model selection or control plane ever routes anything outside the pinned region for inference computations?

Also, we need SOC2 Type II report and a standard NDA (I'll send to procurement). If you can include a DocuSign link for the NDA, that helps speed things up.

Regards,
John Miller
Head of Platform Security
Acme Bank
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: John Miller <john.miller@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Region pinning & data residency (post-call recap)

Hi John —

Appreciate the specifics — we're aligned on the high-level approach. Answers to your questions and notes on implementation: 

- Per-customer region pinning: Yes — Redwood supports region pinning at the customer/account level. We also support routing policies at the route/model level so certain endpoints can be pinned independently.

- Control plane vs runtime: The control plane (metadata, deployments) can be in a central management region, but inference computation and all customer data (requests, embeddings, KV cache) will be pinned to the configured region. Model binaries may be cached in the region; there is no customer content leaving the pinned region for inference.

- Cross-region failover & backups: We support a cold backup pattern where encrypted backups are replicated to a DR region. Backups can be encrypted with customer-managed KMS (we integrate with Azure/AWS KMS and HSM options). We will not perform live inference from the DR backups unless you authorize a manual failover.

- Retention & purge: Default retention can be configured to 90 days for prompt/content. We provide on-demand purge APIs and can support higher retention if required. Logs/audit can be retained for 180 days; we can export logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding.

- No training: Redwood does not use customer inference data for training or model updates without explicit opt-in.

I've attached an updated region-pinning diagram and a proposed data-retention table that maps to your ask. Also linking our SOC2 summary and a HubSpot deal record for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-2027-001

If this looks good, propose we schedule a 45-minute security review next week. What days/times work for your team?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: region-pinning-diagram.pdf, data-retention-table.xlsx

Hi John / Aditya —

Thanks — one small technical note from our infra team: during failover testing we recommend a brief maintenance window for cache warm-up if you elect to bring up the DR region for live inference. Cold backups are fine, but application-level caches (KV cache) will need time to repopulate which can impact latency for a short period.

If procurement is in the loop, happy to provide a short checklist for the legal/security teams listing required artifacts (SOC2, encryption details, SLA language) to help speed review.

I'm available Wed 2027-05-11 09:00–12:00 UTC or Thu 2027-05-12 14:00–16:00 UTC for the security deep-dive. Does either window work for you?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
